The Summit League tournament champions | bowl = [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] | bowl_result = Round of 64 }} {{2010–11 The Summit League men's basketball standings}} The '''2010–11 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team''' were a [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] [[college basketball]] team representing [[Oakland University]]. OU won the conference regular season and [[2011 Summit League men's basketball tournament|conference tournament]] title for the second consecutive year. Oakland received [[The Summit League]]'s automatic berth into the [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] as a #13 seed against #4 seeded [[2010–11 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]]. The Golden Grizzlies lost the game 85–81. ==Preseason== Oakland was picked to win The Summit League championship.[http://www.thesummitleague.org/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=3900&ATCLID=205014838 ] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110103204809/http://www.thesummitleague.org/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=3900&ATCLID=205014838 |date=January 3, 2011 }} They received 29 of 34 first place votes. Center [[Keith Benson]] was picked as the Preseason Conference Player of the Year and named to the All-League First Team. Guard Larry Wright was named to the Second Team. Joining the team for the 2010–11 season were guards [[Reggie Hamilton (basketball)|Reggie Hamilton]] and [[Travis Bader]]. Hamilton was eligible to play after sitting out the [[2009–10 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|2009–10]] season. Hamilton had transferred from fellow conference team [[UMKC Kangaroos men's basketball|UMKC]]. Freshman Bader began playing after his [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] season. Also seeing significant minutes was freshman guard Ryan Bass. ==Regular season== Oakland was the first Division I school to clinch the conference championship.[http://www.thesummitleague.org/fls/3900/sports/mbball/release.pdf ] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120304221125/http://www.thesummitleague.org/fls/3900/sports/mbball/release.pdf |date=March 4, 2012 }} Oakland finished the season with a 34–2 record in their last 36 conference games spanning two seasons, which was the best in NCAA Division I. ===Records=== Oakland set The Summit League's record for most consecutive regular season conference wins with 17. The [[2009–10 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|2009–10 Oakland team]] tied the same record last year, which was originally set by Cleveland State during 1991–92 and 1992–93 seasons. Oakland won three more games before losing to IUPUI to set the record at 20 consecutive regular season conference wins. Benson set The Summit League record for career blocked shots with 371. He passed the mark of 317 set by [[Keith Closs]] of [[Central Connecticut State University]] from 1994–98. ===Player of the Week=== Benson won the conference's player of the week away three times this season (November 29, December 20 and January 24). Point guard Reggie Hamilton won the award twice (January 18 and February 14). ===All-league awards=== Benson was named the conference's Player of the Year and coach Greg Kampe was named Coach of the Year. Both won the awards for the second consecutive season.{{cite web |url=http://www.ougrizzlies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030311aai.html |title=Oakland University Golden Grizzlies Official Athletic Site - Men's Basketball |publisher=Ougrizzlies.com |date=March 3, 2011 |accessdate=February 20, 2014 |archive-date=February 23, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140223071137/http://www.ougrizzlies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030311aai.html |url-status=dead }} Benson and junior guard Reggie Hamilton were named to the All-League First Team. Senior forward [[Will Hudson (basketball)|Will Hudson]] was selected for the Second Team, freshman guard Bader was named to the All-Newcomer Team and senior guard Larry Wright was named the Sixth Man of the Year. Benson was also named The Summit League's Defensive Player of the Year. ===Roster=== {| class="wikitable" style="font-size: 90%;" |- !
